Replace.Text: Plans the districts with the highest weighted adjacency bonus for one city, several cities or new city sites, and marks them with map tacks.

Plans districts for one city, for several cities together (wonders included) and for new city sites. Under your yield weights it looks for the plan with the highest adjacency bonus: small problems are solved exhaustively, larger ones by a search that reports how far the result may be from the best. Preview the plan, then place it as map tacks with district icons; undo is kept with the save. Placement rules and bonuses come from Detailed Map Tacks, so they match what its tacks show. Built districts and your own map tacks are never moved. Requires Detailed Map Tacks. Do not enable together with another district planner such as Auto Map Tacks Planner.

Count the yields of the tiles the districts take, as the tiles give with their best improvement; chopping and harvesting are done before building. Tile yields are weighed by fixed numbers, not by the weights above: Food and Production 1, Science and Culture 5/6, Faith 1/2, Gold 1/4 (1 Production = 4 Gold = 2 Faith), and the same for the one-time yields of chopping and harvesting.

Let districts go on tiles of your other cities: in Manage Citizens, Swap gives such a tile to this city (no district or wonder on it, not next to that city's center).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gain: more adjacency, measured at +13% on average for one city and +20% for several.[NEWLINE]Cost: about three in ten districts need a swap by hand; the other city loses that tile; several cities take about twice as long to plan.

Shows on the map where one district is good: every tile where it can go, shaded from the best down, with the bonus of placing it there alone.

Reach: lets the plan count districts whose buildings help nearby cities, such as Factories, Power Plants, Zoos, Stadiums and Aquariums. Each of your cities or City Center map tacks newly covered adds this many points; a city a district of the same kind already covers does not count. 0 leaves it out.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Gain: covered cities get those buildings' regional effects (Production, Amenities). Measured planning one city on 42 real cities: at weight 1, 3 of them covered more cities; at weight 3, 6.[NEWLINE]Cost: those cities lost 0 to 3 adjacency (up to 4 at weight 3); planning takes about 5% longer.

How many specialty districts this city should plan, required ones included. Above the required number the rest are picked from the pool (best gain first), and three plans with different districts are offered. At the required number nothing is picked.
How many specialty districts each city of this list should plan, required ones included. Above the required number the solver picks the rest from the pool for each city.

Must: always placed. Pool: when the count is above the required number, the best of the pool are picked. Off: left out. Districts are compared by weighted adjacency, plus land, reach and distance when on, plus Housing for Neighborhoods and Preserves (and tile yields for a Must Preserve). Encampments and Aerodromes have no adjacency bonus and are never picked from the pool: make them Must. Districts limited to one per empire (Government Plaza, Diplomatic Quarter) are Must or Off only.

These districts have no Population requirement and do not count toward the number. Auto: added when the city needs it, placed by the solver. An Aqueduct when the city lacks fresh water (its water Housing is below the 5 a River or Lake gives); a Dam when 3 or more free Floodplains tiles lie in its 3 rings (Gathering Storm only). Left out, with a note, when it fits nowhere.

The plan's districts get adjacency bonuses from adjacent Woods and Rainforest; removing them later loses those bonuses. Placing the plan also puts a reminder tack (with the Remove Feature icon) on those tiles, named with what removing them would cost; undo removes these tacks too.

Distance cost: each district and wonder loses this weight times (tiles to your nearest City Center - 1), in the same unit as adjacency; 0 is off. The game does not charge more for distant districts; distant tiles join the city later or cost more Gold to purchase. This expresses a wish to keep districts close.
Click to switch this site on or off. Left out, no districts are planned for it and it is not counted as a new city; the tack stays where it is and still counts as a neighbor.
How many specialty districts each site is scored with. With more ticked, each site picks its best ones; otherwise all of them count.

{1_Rules}[NEWLINE]When ticked, the pool never gives one city both; a city that already has one (built, with a map tack, or Must) does not get the other. Only when the count cannot be filled otherwise are both picked, and the result says so. Must districts are placed as asked.
the {1_Building} gives no Trade Route capacity

Housing: points per Housing. In each city, each Housing up to the population its planned districts need counts 1, each one after it half the one before. A Neighborhood's or Preserve's Housing depends on the Appeal of its tile. With the Preserve set to Must, the yields its Grove and Sanctuary give to adjacent unimproved tiles count too, with each yield's weight (with Land loss on, only on tiles the city works); when it is picked from the pool they are shown, not scored. The plan changes Appeal: a Holy Site or Theater Square gives adjacent tiles +1, an Industrial Zone or Encampment -1, and removing Woods -1 to the tiles around it.

Farms, Pastures and similar improvements give +0.5 Housing each; the city's total is rounded down. Districts of the plan on such tiles cost the city this much Housing. Shown for information; not part of the plan's score.
